title.en: State and use the properties of expectation
Decide whether a game is fair

say.en: A fair stall offers 10 rupees for two heads, 4 rupees for one head, and takes 6 rupees for no head. Should you play? Mathematical expectation answers this. In this lesson: Define mathematical expectation.
State and use the properties of expectation.
Decide whether a game is fair.

body.en: The *mathematical expectation* (expected value, mean) of a discrete random variable is $E(X) = \sum x\,p(x)$; for a continuous one, $E(X) = \int x f(x)\,dx$. It is the long-run average value of X over many repetitions. In a game, if the expected gain of the player is zero the game is fair.

narration.en: The expectation of X is the sum of x times p of x. It is the long-run average. A game is fair if the expected gain is zero.
narration.kn: X ನ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷೆ = Σ x·p(x). ಇದು ದೀರ್ಘಾವಧಿಯ ಸರಾಸರಿ. ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿತ ಲಾಭ ಶೂನ್ಯವಾದರೆ ಆಟ ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ.

narration.en: A stall game: pay a fee to roll a die, win a prize on a six. Your gain X is (prize − fee) with probability 1/6 and −fee with probability 5/6, so E(X) = prize/6 − fee. Play 1000 rounds: the average gain (yellow) settles at E(X). The game is fair when E(X) = 0.

say.en: A stall game: pay a fee to roll a die, win a prize on a six. Your gain X is (prize - fee) with probability 1 over 6 and -fee with probability 5 over 6, so EX equals prize/6 - fee. Play 1000 rounds: the average gain yellow settles at EX. The game is fair when EX equals 0.

body.en: For constants a, b and random variables X, Y: $E(c) = c$; $E(aX) = aE(X)$; $E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b$; addition theorem $E(X + Y) = E(X) + E(Y)$; multiplication theorem $E(XY) = E(X)\,E(Y)$ when X and Y are independent.

narration.en: Expectation of a constant is the constant. E of a X plus b is a E X plus b. E of X plus Y is E X plus E Y, and for independent variables E of X Y is E X times E Y.
narration.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕದ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಅದೇ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕ. E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b. E(X + Y) = E(X) + E(Y); ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ಚರಗಳಿಗೆ E(XY) = E(X)E(Y).

say.en: Expectation of a constant is the constant. E of a X plus b is a E X plus b. E of X plus Y is E X plus E Y, and for independent variables E of X Y is E X times E Y. EaX plus b equals aEX plus b.
say.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕದ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಅದೇ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕ. EaX plus b equals aEX plus b. EX plus Y equals EX plus EY; ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ಚರಗಳಿಗೆ EXY equals EXEY.

say.en: EX plus Y equals EX plus EY.
EXY equals EXEY if independent.

problem.en: A die is thrown. X is the number shown. Find E(X) and E(2X + 3).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A die is thrown. X is the number shown. Find E(X) and E(2X + 3).

say.en: Let us work this out together. A die is thrown. X is the number shown. Find EX and E2X plus 3.
EX equals (1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 5 plus 6) times 1 over 6 equals 21 over 6 equals 3.5.
E2X plus 3 equals 2EX plus 3 equals 23.5 plus 3 equals 10.
So the answer is EX equals 3.5, E2X plus 3 equals 10.
